chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ismail ibn Mihran from Ali ibn Abu Hamza from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about the woman who dies while the child is moving in her belly: should her belly be split open and her child extracted? He said: Yes. And in the narration of Ibn Abi Umayr, there is an addition: the child is extracted and her belly is stitched up.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling if a pregnant woman dies but the fetus is still alive in her womb?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'salvation of the fetus' (kharaj al-janin) in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the preservation of the unborn child's life over the integrity of the mother's body after death. The addition from Ibn Abi Umayr specifying that the abdomen is stitched after extraction reflects the practical medical and legal procedures developed by scholars to ensure the child's survival and dignity. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the fetus as an independent legal entity with a right to life, even if the mother has already passed away.
